blocks.text: The conflict in the synagogue concerns particular Jewish leaders who watch Jesus and later join the Herodians in planning against him. It should not be used to assign collective guilt to Jewish people, to portray Judaism as uniquely hypocritical or hard-hearted, or to support antisemitism.

Mark 3:20-35 begins with Jesus’ family seeking him, interrupts that scene with the scribes’ accusation and Jesus’ response, and then returns to his family outside the house. Mark repeatedly uses this kind of nested arrangement, in which the two episodes are read alongside one another. Here, the return to the family scene invites readers to consider Jesus’ definition of his true family in the light of the dispute that precedes it.

sections.title: A story set within a story
